question.text: As per SCRA, the definition of 'derivative' includes which of the following?

answer.text: All of: a security derived from a debt instrument, share, loan, risk instrument or contract for differences; a contract deriving value from prices or index of prices of underlying securities; commodity derivatives; and such other instruments as the Central Government may declare
A security derived from a debt instrument, share, or loan
A contract deriving its value from prices or index of prices of underlying securities

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SCRA, 'derivative' includes: (i) a security derived from a debt instrument, share, loan (secured or unsecured), risk instrument or contract for differences; (ii) a contract that derives its value from prices or an index of prices of underlying securities; (iii) commodity derivatives; and (iv) such other instruments as may be declared by the Central Government. The correct option captures the full statutory definition. The Trap: Each single-category distractor is correct but incomplete. SCRA's definition is intentionally broad, covering derivatives over debt, shares, loans, contracts for differences, indices, commodities and any other instrument the Central Government may notify. Note: Replaced the answer-randomization-fragile 'All of the above' wording with a standalone comprehensive option that mirrors the SCRA definition, and removed the pro-tip line that was not source-grounded.
